newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Karachi bourse to mull CLA directives on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Karachi bourse to mull CLA directives on Friday.

text.p: Pakistan's main Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) said on Thursday it would discuss on Friday directives from the state Corporate Law Authority (CLA) for restructuring its board of directors.
CLA chairman Sahmim Ahmed Khan said earlier the CLA had told the KSE to change the composition of its board to bring in professionals not involved in the equity market.
"We have already two non-broker members in our board who are represented by the NIT (National Investment Trust) and ICP (Investment Corporation of Pakistan)," KSE president Arif Habib told Reuters.
"The concept is there... (and) the CLA wants to increase this number," he said.

A CLA directive said the governing boards of the directors of the stock exchanges should be restructured to enable induction of at least 33 percent outside non-broker members representing public interest to be nominated by the CLA.
Habib said KSE's board of directors would review CLA's directives at a meeting on Friday.
"We are already working to modernise the stock exchange and some of our projects have been completed or are near completion," he said.
Habib said similar instructions would soon be sent to Pakistan's two other bourses -- the Lahore Stock Exchange and the Islamabad Stock Exchange.
